reasons: This is not a duplicate of prior_flow_atlas. I checked run_flow_atlas.py: its 18 day types are weekdays, gotobi, month-start and month-end ordinals, and US, Japan and England holidays. There is no calendar-month condition, and its windows are at most 8 hours, so a two-month seasonal was outside its search space. The atlas's Bonferroni bar (t >= 3.7) covers re-slices of that space, not a single pre-registered replication of a published anomaly. prior_trend_follow and prior_index_meanrev did not condition on month either.

The primary arm does not match the published claim. The rationale cites Baur (2013) for positive returns concentrated in September and November, yet the primary window is sep_oct, which includes October and drops November. A confirmatory test must test what was published (September and November), or the replication is itself a choice made after the fact.

mar_apr is not a clean control. Indian physical demand has a second peak around Akshaya Tritiya (April-May) and the spring wedding season, so March-April is not a no-demand season under the hypothesis's own mechanism. Kill rule (2) is meant to separate seasonal demand from gold's general drift in the same years. The right comparison is every other month of the same years (the rest of the year, Mon-Thu, same 24-hour structure).

Executor mismatch that silently halves and biases the sample. The rules exit on E(D_next), so the position closes at the open of the bar after E(D_next). At the close of E(D_next) the position is still open, and the executor ignores entries while a position is open (executor.py: 'register this bar's signals (ignored while a position is open)'). Every second day is therefore skipped, and the trades fall on Mondays and Wednesdays only. The sample halves to about 150 design trades and a day-of-week pattern enters that the hypothesis never registered. The text accepts 'the day is skipped', but here it is systematic, not occasional.

Power and usefulness. By its own numbers (+0.02 to +0.04 R per trade, per-trade sd about 0.4 R at a 2 x ATR stop, about 280 trades), design t is about 1.0-1.7. It can reach the programme's t >= 2 bar only if the effect is larger than the literature suggests. Even if real, Sep + Nov at about 35 trades a year x 0.03 R is about 1 R a year, a minor contributor to a +10% phase. It is cheap and a clean out-of-sample reading of a published anomaly, so it is worth a small amount of compute. The Director should expect an honest negative or a sub-bar positive.

Long-only on gold carries luck risk. Long-only tests on rising assets pass the bar 2-8% of the time. 2024-2026 is a strong gold bull market, so a positive holdout from a long-only gold rule is weak evidence by itself. The seasonal claim must be judged as the window minus the control, in check and in the holdout, not as raw avg R.

Costs are negligible. Spread plus slippage of about 34 pips against a 2 x ATR20 stop of about 4500 pips is under 0.01 R. One night of financing at policy rate + 1% on a 2-3% stop distance is about 0.003 R.
revisions: 1) Windows: "sep_nov_baur" = D in September or November (the published months; primary), "sep_nov" = September 1 to November 30 (the broader physical-demand season), "rest" = every other month (January-August and December; the control). Drop sep_oct and mar_apr. Grid: window x sl_atr [1.0, 2.0] = 6 combinations. Default window = sep_nov_baur, sl_atr = 2.0. 2) Kill rule (1) moves to sep_nov_baur at sl_atr = 2.0. Kill rule (2) becomes: in design, avg R(sep_nov_baur) - avg R(rest) >= 0.02 at the same stop, otherwise kill regardless of sign. Kill rule (4) adds: in check, avg R(window) - avg R(rest) > 0 at the chosen combination. If promoted, the holdout verdict must also report the window-minus-rest difference, and a holdout where the window does not beat the rest is a fail even if raw avg R > 0. Pre-register this now. 3) Kill rule (3), seasons not days: at least 5 of 8 design seasons (Sep + Nov R sum per year) positive. Keep it. 4) Exit: set exit_long on the last bar before E(D_next), not on E(D_next). The trade then closes at the open of the bar ending at 20:00 UTC on D_next (about a 23-hour hold), the position is flat when the next day's signal registers at E(D_next), and every Mon-Thu day in the window trades. Minimum design trades: 250 for sep_nov_baur. 5) Update expectations: design t 1.0-1.7 is accepted as below the pass bar. Register that a pass needs design t >= 2, which this test reaches only if the effect is stronger than published.
notes_for_builder: H1 bars are labelled by open time. E(D) is the last bar on UTC date D whose close (ts + 1h) is in (16:00, 20:00] UTC, normally the bar opening 19:00. Window membership uses the UTC month of D. window is a string param read from p['window'], with values sep_nov_baur (months 9 and 11), sep_nov (months 9-11) and rest (months 1-8 and 12); raise on any other value. Weekday of D must be Mon-Thu. ATR: daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, 20))[E(D)]; skip if NaN or <= 0. Entry: entry_long[E(D)] = True, type 0, valid_bars 1, sl_dist = sl_atr * ATR, tp NaN, max_bars = 30. Exit: let X = E(D_next), where D_next is the next UTC date with a valid E (any weekday, including Friday). Set exit_long[X - 1] = True only if X - 1 > E(D) (oracle pattern exit_long[xi - 1]). Do not add an entry on Fridays or weekends. Loop over dates, not bars. No other filters.
